result:
Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDatePrinterAgentTest.java` — a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (matching the project's JUnit Jupiter 5.14.4 usage) with 35 test methods covering:

- Constructor null-argument handling (pattern/timeZone NPE, locale falling back to default)
- Getters and timezone-clone isolation
- `format` overloads for `Date`, `Calendar`, `long`, with `StringBuilder`/`StringBuffer` append semantics
- Calendar cloning/re-zoning behavior when the calendar's timezone differs from the printer's
- Package-private `format(Object)` and deprecated `format(Object, StringBuffer, FieldPosition)`/`applyRules` paths, including the unsupported-type `IllegalArgumentException`
- Pattern letter coverage: year truncation/padding, month (`M`/`L`), weekday (`E`/`u`), 12/24-hour boundary cases at midnight/afternoon, milliseconds, era, timezone name/number (`z`/`Z`), ISO-8601 (`X`) including the invalid `XXXX` case
- Quoted literals with escaped apostrophes, and illegal pattern components
- `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, `getMaxLengthEstimate`
- Serialization round-trip (exercising the transient-field reinit in `readObject`)
- The package-private static helpers `getTimeZoneDisplay` and `clear()`
- The `parseToken` method directly

All tests compile under `--release 8` without lambdas/diamond operators/try-with-resources, and the full `./_tools/test.sh` run passes (35/35).
